name: poll_request_completion_status
description: Reads a request record through a stored pointer and copies its header into a local buffer. It marks the record as acknowledged when a type and state pair match, and returns zero only when a second type and state pair matches, otherwise one.

name: run_setup_sequence_until_ready
description: Runs a fixed series of setup calls that configure a display or device, repeating one query until it returns a nonzero value. It then stores a constant in a global field and makes one final setup call with it.

name: copy_picture_rows_to_buffer
description: Copies a counted list of 40-byte picture rows from a source table into a buffer, locating each row from the width and offset arguments. It then passes the buffer, a size derived from one argument, and a bit value derived from the row count to a drawing call.

name: emit_packed_word_fields
description: Walks a range of 16-bit words, splitting each into a high byte and two four-bit fields. Each set of fields is passed with the position index to a library routine.

name: reset_thirty_two_entries
description: Calls one library routine for each index from zero to thirty-one, passing zeros as the remaining arguments. This resets a block of thirty-two consecutive entries.

name: forward_global_handle_to_routine
description: Passes a global handle to one further routine and returns. It is a thin wrapper that adds no logic of its own.

name: forward_global_handle_to_library
description: Passes a global handle to a routine that calls a library vector at a fixed offset from the library base. It adds no logic of its own.

name: select_record_and_set_mode
description: Reads a 16-byte table entry chosen by the argument and passes its fields to a routine. For argument two it stores a global value in a handle field and calls a second routine with a stored constant; for argument three it clears that field and calls it with zero.

name: forward_library_call_132
description: Loads a library base from a global and calls the routine 132 bytes below that base, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: forward_library_call_198
description: Loads a library base from a global and calls the routine 198 bytes below that base, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: format_string_to_output
description: Walks a printf-style format string, copying literal bytes and collapsing doubled percent signs. Each conversion is expanded by a helper into a scratch area, and every output byte is sent through a callback or a bounded buffer.

name: open_timer_device_request
description: Creates a message port and an I/O request block, then opens timer.device with that request. If the port or request cannot be made, or the open fails, it cleans up and reports an error code through a helper.

name: prepare_timer_request_block
description: Fills a timer request block with command code nine, zeroes one field, and stores a value in another. It then passes the block to a library routine.

name: release_request_structure
description: For a non-null argument, passes the structure's embedded pointer to a helper if it is set, then calls a library routine on the structure. A second routine is then called on it with zero.

name: release_two_global_handles
description: Calls one library routine on the handle at offset eight, then on the handle at offset four, then on the first handle again. The three calls run in sequence.

name: open_input_device_request
description: Creates a message port and an I/O request block, then opens input.device with that request. When the open succeeds it runs two further library calls on the port and request, and reports an error code on failure.

name: send_control_request_with_buffers
description: Runs a library call with a size of 256 for each of two handles, fills a request block on the stack with a command code and a pointer, and sends it. It then makes two further library calls with a size constant.

name: apply_mode_table_entry
description: Applies the 16-byte table entry selected by the argument, clamping any index above one to zero. When a global flag is set it also stores the mode in a request block and sends it.

name: store_bit_mask_result
description: Computes a single-bit mask from a byte held in a structure reached through a global, and passes that mask to a routine. The routine's result is then passed to a second routine together with a structure field.

name: run_winter_intro_animation
description: Loads the winter picture files and sets up colour and timing tables, then draws sprite rows in staged loops. It finishes with a timed animation loop of up to one thousand steps, after which the timing and input resources are reset.

name: draw_winter_frame_sprites
description: Draws a set of sprites at positions derived from two timing counters, using one of two layouts depending on a flag. It then waits until a timer value reaches a fixed threshold before drawing a final sprite.

name: repeat_routine_by_count
description: Calls one routine repeatedly, the number of times given by the argument, and returns.

name: fill_global_table_entries
description: Calls a routine twenty times and stores each result into successive entries of a global table. It then calls a routine once for each index up to a count held in a global, and finally forwards its two parameters to another routine.

name: build_sprite_entry_table
description: Fills a table of 34-byte entries, one per item in four groups whose sizes come from a global array, linking each entry to its position and a pointer. It then sets a series of flag and character fields in a fixed structure.

name: retry_library_until_nonzero
description: Calls a library routine repeatedly with a global argument until it returns a nonzero result.

name: mark_list_entry_character
description: Follows a linked list from a head pointer for a given number of steps, then writes either a space or an asterisk into that node's text buffer, depending on the flag argument.

name: copy_bytes_forward
description: Copies the given number of bytes one at a time from a source buffer to a destination buffer.

name: store_long_in_linked_field
description: Writes a 32-bit value into a field of the structure that a pointer at offset twenty-six of the argument refers to.

name: forward_library_call_30
description: Calls the library routine 30 bytes below the base stored in a global, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: forward_library_call_54
description: Calls the library routine 54 bytes below the base stored in a global, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: forward_library_call_66
description: Calls the library routine 66 bytes below the base stored in a global, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: forward_library_call_72
description: Calls the library routine 72 bytes below the base stored in a global, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: forward_library_call_228
description: Calls the library routine 228 bytes below the base held in a global, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: forward_library_call_240
description: Calls the library routine 240 bytes below the base held in a global, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: forward_library_call_246
description: Calls the library routine 246 bytes below the base held in a global, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: forward_library_call_252
description: Calls the library routine 252 bytes below the base held in a global, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: forward_library_call_264
description: Calls the library routine 264 bytes below the base held in a global, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: forward_library_call_270
description: Calls the library routine 270 bytes below the base held in a global, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: forward_library_call_282
description: Calls the library routine 282 bytes below the base held in a global, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: forward_library_call_354
description: Calls the library routine 354 bytes below the base held in a global, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: allocate_five_game_buffers
description: Allocates five buffers of 2560, 260, 36, 160 and 1024 bytes with memory-type flags, reporting an error code if any allocation fails. It then saves one field of the current task and replaces it with a stored pointer.

name: call_routine_with_fallback
description: Calls a routine with the fixed argument four and two stored values, then subtracts one from its result. When that difference is zero it returns the result of a second routine instead.

name: request_numbered_resource
description: Makes a library call with two stored pointers, the identifier 1830 and a flag of one, and passes any nonzero result to a second routine. It has no other logic.

name: call_with_fallback_five
description: Calls a routine with the fixed argument five and two stored values, then subtracts one from its result. When that difference is zero it returns the result of a second routine instead.

name: run_menu_selection_loop
description: Prepares two stack buffers from its arguments, then reads input codes in a loop until one of three exit codes arrives. Codes twelve and thirteen move the highlighted row up or down, and the routine returns the code that ended the loop.

name: run_slot_selection_loop
description: Runs the same row-selection loop as its sibling, using stack-held buffers instead of arguments. Its text reference names a .slt data file.

name: refill_selection_list_rows
description: Fills six row entries with pointers into the item table, then redraws the list. It processes the same cursor codes as the selection loop.

name: run_selection_loop_body
description: Runs one pass of the selection loop: refreshes the list rows, handles the movement codes, and issues redraw calls. It returns once an exit code has been read.

name: draw_frame_around_structure
description: Computes a rectangle from fields of a stored structure, offset by fixed amounts, and passes its four coordinates to a drawing routine.

name: draw_rectangle_border
description: When a stored item is present, fills a rectangle inside the given corners and draws its outline with eight line-drawing calls.

name: redraw_stored_item_region
description: Runs three setup calls, then calls routines on the stored item's field and on a second global offset to redraw its region.

name: bracket_routine_with_handle_calls
description: Brackets a call to another routine between two calls on a stored handle, one passing zero beforehand and one passing minus one afterwards. It returns that routine's result.

name: forward_library_call_174
description: Passes two global pointers and a global address to a library routine 174 bytes below the library base, then returns.

name: scan_directory_entries_into_table
description: Skips leading spaces in a path, locks it, and reads its directory entries into a table of up to seventy-eight names. It sets a flag when an entry has one particular type code, and unlocks the path when the table is full.

name: read_directory_listing_checked
description: Locks a path and reports an error code, returning one, if the lock fails. Otherwise it reads directory entries in a loop, storing each name into a table until the table is full or an entry is rejected.

name: collect_directory_entries
description: Reads directory entries in a loop, storing each name and its flag into a table. It stops at the end of the listing or when the table holds seventy-nine entries.

name: store_directory_entry_name
description: Stores each directory entry name in a table, clamping a length to twenty-two characters when it is too large. It is the storage step shared by the listing routines.

name: read_next_directory_entries
description: Repeatedly fetches the next directory entry, storing its name and length into a table of 32-byte rows. It stops when the table is full or the end-of-directory code arrives.

name: read_directory_in_batches
description: Repeats a batch of directory-entry reads, resetting a counter at each pass. It returns zero at the end of the listing and three when the table is full.

name: read_listing_then_unlock
description: Repeats a batch read of directory entries while a lock is held, and releases the lock when the listing ends.

name: unlock_listing_and_return
description: Unlocks the lock held in the frame and returns three to its caller.

name: restore_saved_task_field
description: Writes a saved pointer back into a field of the current task, undoing the earlier replacement made by the buffer allocation routine.

name: build_game_file_path
description: Builds a full path from a directory and a file name, adds a separator when needed, then locks the result. Its text references name the .slt, .solo, .tour and .trn file types and the game title.

name: read_or_write_data_file
description: Opens a file through a library call chosen by the mode argument, then reads or writes a block of data with it. It reports an I/O error through a helper if one of the calls fails.

name: request_resource_in_current_dir
description: Locks the current directory, makes the numbered resource request with the given pointer, then unlocks the directory. It reports the returned code through a helper when the request gives a nonzero result. Its text reference names a .solo file.

name: check_table_sum_after_request
description: Sums a global array before and after a numbered resource request, and calls a routine when the two totals differ. It reports a request failure through a helper.

name: check_table_sum_against_stored
description: Makes the numbered resource request, then sums a global array and compares the total with a stored value. It calls a routine when the two differ.

name: compare_stored_totals
description: Compares two stored totals and calls a routine when they differ, then calls a second routine.

name: apply_stored_option_settings
description: Reads several stored option flags and selects matching setup calls for each one, then loops over four slots. It finishes by applying the chosen configuration through a sequence of routine calls.

name: invoke_record_for_large_key
description: Searches a table of three-field records for a matching key value. When the key is above ninety-nine and a match is found, it passes that record's stored pointer to a routine.

name: lookup_record_and_invoke
description: Searches the same record table for a matching key and passes the matching record's stored pointer to a routine.

name: invoke_record_when_within_count
description: Passes a field of a stored record to a routine when one counter value is at most another.

name: find_name_in_entry_table
description: Searches a table of 32-byte entries for a name, comparing characters without regard to case, and returns one when a match is found. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: match_entry_name_characters
description: Walks table entries from a start index, comparing each entry's characters with a target name without regard to case. It sets a match flag when one matches and stops the scan.

name: return_match_flag
description: Returns the match flag stored in the caller's frame, which the name search sets.

name: convert_char_to_uppercase
description: Returns the byte unchanged unless it is a lowercase letter, in which case it returns the matching uppercase letter.

name: accumulate_file_info_value
description: Locks a named path and reads its information block into a 36-byte buffer. When the value in the block is three or less and a stored flag is set, it adds that value to a running total, then releases the lock.

name: forward_library_call_42
description: Calls the library routine 42 bytes below the base stored in a global, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: forward_library_call_150
description: Calls the library routine 150 bytes below the base stored in a global, then returns. It has no other logic.

name: open_audio_device_channels
description: Allocates a 1496-byte block and a message port, reporting an error code of 400 if either fails. It fills twenty-two channel records with default values, then sets up the audio.device request with them.

name: release_audio_resources
description: Does nothing when a stored flag is set. Otherwise it runs a teardown call, releases two stored handles, then releases each of ten stored pointers that is non-null.

name: release_audio_handles_and_list
description: Runs a teardown call, releases the two stored handles, then releases each of ten stored pointers that is non-null.

name: start_sound_voices
description: Clamps a level argument to three and picks five or nine voices from it. It frees every channel bit held in the mask, then allocates free channel bits for each voice and sends an audio request for each.

name: start_sound_from_table
description: Clamps a level argument to eight, releases the channel bits held in the mask, then allocates free channel bits for each entry of the table selected by that level. It sends an audio request for each allocated channel.

name: wait_until_sound_channels_free
description: Sets fixed values and flag bits in an audio request, then loops while channel bits remain set. Each pass releases finished channels and issues a command for the channels still in use.

name: silence_remaining_sound_channels
description: Repeatedly issues a command for the channel mask and clears the bits of finished requests until no channel bits remain set.

name: return_without_effect
description: Contains no code and returns immediately, so it has no effect on memory or hardware.

name: create_message_port_block
description: Allocates a signal bit and a 34-byte port block, returning zero if either fails. It fills in the block's type, signal bit and current task, then either initialises a message list or adds the port to a global list.

name: delete_message_port_block
description: Removes the port from its list when it is linked, marks its status fields as deleted, frees its signal bit and releases the block.

name: dispatch_input_messages
description: Waits for an input message in a loop and replies to messages of one particular type code. Other messages are copied into a 52-byte buffer, and a table of stored values is scanned to match the message's code.

name: advance_sequence_on_match
description: Checks an incoming message's state against the expected entry in a table and advances the sequence index on a match. When the flag is clear it resets the index, and when the sequence completes it sets a timeout and a mode value.

name: return_without_effect
description: Contains no code and returns immediately, so it has no effect on memory or hardware.

name: advance_sequence_on_match
description: Checks an incoming message's state against the expected entry in a table and advances the sequence index on a match. When the flag is clear it resets the index, and when the sequence completes it sets a timeout and a mode value.

name: scan_input_table_entries
description: Resets the sequence index when a flag is clear, then waits for input messages in a loop. It replies to one message type and scans a table of stored values for each other message.

name: scan_game_file_entries
description: Walks a list of file entries, comparing each name with a directory listing built from the examine and parent-directory calls. Its text references name the .slt and .trn file types it looks for.

name: call_routine_and_return
description: Calls one routine with no arguments and returns.

name: append_string_at_end
description: Finds the current length of a buffer by calling a helper with the first argument, then copies a null-terminated string from the second argument to the end of the buffer. It returns the first argument unchanged.

name: copy_string_with_limit
description: Copies a string into a buffer at the position given by a length helper, stopping at the null terminator or after a given count of bytes. It then writes a terminating zero and returns the first argument unchanged.

name: expand_format_into_pointer
description: Walks a printf-style format string using a pointer held in the argument, handling doubled percent signs and conversions through a helper. Each output byte is written through the pointer, and a callback takes over when the output count runs out.

name: initialise_list_header
description: Points a list header at itself: its head is set to the field just after the header, its tail word is cleared, and its tail pointer refers back to the header.

name: count_string_length
description: Counts the bytes from a given pointer offset up to the terminating zero byte, and returns that count.

name: transfer_buffer_for_stream
description: Checks the state flags of a stream structure, then calls a transfer routine with its buffer and count. It sets error or end flags from the result, and returns minus one when the stream cannot be used.

name: transfer_stream_block
description: Checks a stream's flags and starts a buffer transfer, returning minus one when the stream is unusable. It passes the buffer and its count to a transfer routine and returns that result.

name: transfer_stream_with_count
description: Checks the stream flags, then passes the buffer, a count and the stream's values to a transfer routine. It records a negative result as an error flag and a zero result as an end flag.

name: mark_stream_busy_and_transfer
description: Marks a stream as busy, transfers a block through a helper, and sets error and end flags from the result. It returns minus one when the stream is already in use.

name: transfer_stream_without_checks
description: Marks a stream as busy and transfers a block through a helper, without first checking the stream's state flags. It sets error and end flags from the result.

name: read_next_stream_byte
description: Takes the next byte from a stream buffer and decrements its remaining count. When the count runs out it calls a helper to refill the stream instead.

name: forward_stream_to_helper
description: Passes the stream pointer from the frame to a helper routine and returns.

name: write_byte_to_stream
description: Writes one byte into a stream buffer and decrements its room count. When the room is exhausted it calls a flush routine, and it sets flags in the stream state from the result.

name: allocate_stream_buffer
description: Returns minus one when the stream is already flagged. Otherwise it calls a helper with a global pointer, stores the result in the stream's fields, clears the state flags and returns zero.

name: parse_format_specifier
description: Skips an optional minus sign, digits, a decimal point and an 'l' modifier. It then looks up the conversion character in a table and dispatches to its handler, returning zero when the character is not in the table.

name: convert_field_with_width_cap
description: Picks a field width from a state value, defaulting to six and capping it at nineteen. It passes that width to a conversion routine and advances the buffer pointer.

name: format_number_into_field
description: Sets the field width to six when unset and caps it at nineteen. It then calls a conversion routine with the width and the buffer, and advances the output pointer past the result.

name: format_number_with_width
description: Calls a conversion routine with the field width and buffer chosen by the caller, then advances the output pointer past the result.

name: write_fill_characters
description: Writes the fill character repeatedly for a counted number of positions, then stores the output pointer and returns the count plus one.

name: write_padded_field_text
description: Writes fill characters for a counted number of positions, then copies a sequence of characters from a source buffer and stores the output pointer.

name: copy_field_characters
description: Copies a counted number of characters from a source pointer into the output buffer, then stores the output pointer and returns the count plus one.

name: store_pointer_and_return_count
description: Stores a saved pointer into the location referenced by the argument and returns a stored counter plus one.

name: format_number_default_width
description: Sets the field width to six when unset and caps it at nineteen. It then calls a conversion routine with the width and the buffer.

name: format_signed_number_field
description: Formats a number into the field, adjusting its sign and digit count before a helper writes the digits.

name: compute_number_field_length
description: Works out how many characters a number needs by counting its sign and digits. It adds one for values above ninety-nine, one more above nine hundred and ninety-nine, and a fixed amount.

name: pad_number_field_to_width
description: Applies the same length adjustments as its sibling, then writes fill characters to pad the field to the requested width before the digits are written.

name: pad_and_write_number_digits
description: Adjusts the length of a number for values above ninety-nine and above nine hundred and ninety-nine. It writes fill characters before the digits when the field has room.

name: write_decimal_fraction_digits
description: Writes a minus sign when the sign flag is set, then one integer digit or a zero, a decimal point, and the remaining fraction digits.

name: write_integer_and_fraction_digits
description: Writes an integer digit or a zero for each remaining position, then writes fraction digits and pads the rest with zeros.

name: write_zero_padding_digits
description: Writes a zero, then repeatedly writes zeros or leftover digits until the requested count is used up. Fill characters are added when space remains.

name: write_decimal_point_and_digits
description: Writes integer digits while a counter remains, adds a decimal point when a fraction length is set, then writes the fraction digits.

name: write_zero_then_fraction
description: Writes a zero, then the decimal point and fraction digits, stopping when the counters run out.

name: write_fraction_part
description: Writes a decimal point when a fraction length is set, then writes fraction digits and pads with zeros or fill characters when the field has room.

name: write_zeros_with_field_limit
description: Writes zeros while the counters allow, then writes leftover digits and adds fill characters up to the field width.

name: write_digit_then_decimal_point
description: Writes one integer digit or a zero, then a decimal point, then the fraction digits that remain.

name: write_leading_zero_and_point
description: Writes a leading zero and a decimal point, then the fraction digits from the value, stopping when the counter is used up.

name: write_scientific_exponent
description: Writes a zero, then an exponent marker, and the exponent digits with a minus sign where the exponent is negative.

name: write_exponent_marker_and_digits
description: Writes an exponent marker and a plus or minus sign, then converts the exponent into digits held in an eleven-character scratch buffer.

name: write_positive_exponent_digits
description: Writes a plus sign, then converts the exponent value into decimal digits in a scratch buffer and copies them to the output.

name: copy_padding_characters
description: Copies a counted run of padding characters to the output, then stores the output pointer and returns the count plus one.

name: store_pointer_and_return_count
description: Stores a saved pointer into the location referenced by the argument and returns a stored counter plus one.

name: create_io_request_block
description: Allocates a memory block for an I/O request when the first argument is nonzero, setting its type code, size field and device pointer. It returns the block, or zero when the argument is zero or the allocation fails.

name: delete_io_request_block
description: If the pointer is non-null, marks the request's type and two status fields as cleared, then frees the block using its stored size.

name: create_standard_io_request
description: Creates an I/O request of the fixed size forty-eight for the given pointer and returns the result.

name: delete_standard_io_request
description: Passes its pointer argument to a deletion routine and returns with no other work.

name: combine_pair_into_value
description: Calls a routine that fills two values, then returns the first multiplied by two hundred and fifty-six plus the second shifted right by twelve bits.

name: draw_menu_list_items
description: Selects a 30-byte list record and stores a value in its text field. It then walks the linked items, drawing entries whose text starts with a dash as separators and other entries as text, within a height limit.

name: draw_cursor_at_index
description: Computes a cursor position from the current index and a stored offset, then passes that position to two drawing routines.

name: draw_two_panel_frames
description: Draws a pair of framed panels, each built from two coordinate pairs taken from the arguments and fixed sizes of twenty and twenty-three.

name: draw_four_corner_markers
description: Sets a mode value of fifteen, then draws four markers at the corners of a rectangle offset by nineteen and twenty-two units from the given position.

name: return_without_effect
description: Contains no code and returns immediately, so it has no effect on memory or hardware.

name: clear_entry_flag_bit
description: Looks up an entry by index, then clears bit sixteen in its flag word.

name: clear_entry_flags_masked
description: Looks up an entry by index, then clears the bits given by a mask from its flag word. Two library calls bracket the change.

name: find_list_node_at_index
description: Follows the next pointers of a linked list from the head pointer stored at an offset, for the given number of steps. It returns the node reached, or zero when the list ends first.

name: return_without_effect
description: Contains no code and returns immediately, so it has no effect on memory or hardware.

name: store_four_word_fields
description: Writes four 16-bit values into consecutive fields of the record at the pointer argument.

name: return_without_effect
description: Contains no code and returns immediately, so it has no effect on memory or hardware.

name: next_pseudo_random_word
description: Shifts a 32-bit state left by one bit and XORs in a feedback constant when the top bit was set, then returns the low sixteen bits. Each call advances the random sequence.

name: count_list_entries
description: Counts the nodes of the linked list whose head pointer is stored at a fixed offset in the structure argument.

name: draw_entry_when_visible
description: Draws the entry at its stored coordinates when its high flag bit is clear. Otherwise it calls a routine on the entry instead.

name: return_without_effect
description: Contains no code and returns immediately, so it has no effect on memory or hardware.

name: draw_two_screen_bands
description: Draws two horizontal bands across a screen width of 320 units at fixed positions, each followed by a second drawing call.

name: set_entry_highlight_state
description: Sets or clears the high flag bit of an entry, calling library routines when the state changes. It then writes a mode value of thirty-one or six into the entry.

name: draw_three_screen_bands
description: Draws three horizontal bands across a screen width of 320 units at fixed offsets, each followed by a second drawing call.

name: draw_text_string
description: Sets drawing mode values, measures the length of a null-terminated string, then draws the string with a library call.

name: draw_text_with_colour
description: Like its sibling, measures a null-terminated string and draws it, but takes the drawing mode from its second argument.

name: return_without_effect
description: Contains no code and returns immediately, so it has no effect on memory or hardware.

name: forward_two_word_arguments
description: Passes its two 16-bit arguments to a routine and returns.

name: copy_eight_bytes_to_local
description: Copies eight bytes from the source pointer into a local buffer, then returns without using the copy.

name: measure_cell_boundary_distances
description: Measures distances from a position to the neighbouring cell boundaries in a 16-bit table, clamping negative distances to zero. The results select the cells to test, and drawing is done through a library call.

name: compute_cell_overlap_extents
description: Computes the clamped distances from a position to the edges of neighbouring cells in a 16-bit table, then returns the extents derived from them.

name: check_cell_clearance
description: Computes two clamped distances from a cell to its neighbours in a 16-bit table and returns a value based on them.

name: test_point_inside_cell
description: Measures a clamped distance to a neighbouring cell. For one special record code it tests whether a point lies within the record's rectangle.

name: test_rectangle_overlap_clearance
description: Tests whether a candidate point or rectangle lies inside a stored cell rectangle, returning one on a match. The special record code uses a simpler test.

name: test_clearance_for_sprite_edges
description: Tests whether a sprite of the given width fits between the cell's edges, returning one when the clearance is sufficient.

name: test_box_within_cell_bounds
description: Returns one when a box with the given offsets lies within the cell's bounds, otherwise zero.

name: test_top_edge_fit
description: Returns one when a position lies within the cell's horizontal range and the box fits below its top edge, otherwise zero.

name: return_zero_result
description: Returns zero with no other work.

name: lookup_grid_neighbour_value
description: Computes a neighbouring cell index on a fifteen-column grid from a base index and offsets. It returns zero when the index falls outside the grid, and otherwise returns the value stored there.

name: return_without_effect
description: Contains no code and returns immediately, so it has no effect on memory or hardware.

name: mark_entry_and_refresh_rectangle
description: Sets the high flag bit of a sprite entry, computes a rectangle enlarged by a few units around its position and size, and passes it to a drawing routine after a library call.

name: forward_record_position
description: Passes the first two 16-bit fields of a record, together with a further argument, to a routine, then returns.

name: forward_zero_argument
description: Calls one routine with the argument zero and returns.

name: advance_record_position
description: Increments two fields of a record by one, then passes the record and a value to a routine.

name: draw_bordered_frame_pattern
description: Draws a patterned border around a rectangle described by a record, repeating the edge segments once per step of a count derived from a global value.

name: draw_record_rectangle
description: Copies the four 16-bit fields of a record and passes them, with two of them as coordinates, to a drawing routine.

name: draw_layered_record_rectangle
description: Draws a rectangle described by a record in several passes, each with a different mode value, using the record's position and size.

name: clip_and_draw_rectangle
description: Clips a rectangle's width and height to the bounds held in a structure, then passes the clipped values to a drawing routine.

name: store_global_mode_value
description: Stores its argument in a global field that later drawing routines read.

name: return_without_effect
description: Contains no code and returns immediately, so it has no effect on memory or hardware.

name: save_four_blocks_to_file
description: Opens a file through a library call and, when the open succeeds, writes four blocks of 8000 bytes from a table followed by a 32-byte block. It then closes the file.

name: write_blocks_to_open_file
description: Writes four blocks of 8000 bytes taken from a table, then a 32-byte block, to an already open file, and closes it.

name: write_header_and_close
description: Writes a 32-byte block from a global to an open file and then closes it.

name: draw_fixed_marker_set
description: Sets a draw mode of four, then draws a fixed set of eight markers at stored positions offset by fixed amounts.

name: set_flag_when_global_target
description: Sets a global flag to one when the argument points to the global block, and does nothing otherwise.

name: divide_signed_values
description: Divides two signed 32-bit values by restoring division over thirty-two steps. It returns zero when the divisor is zero, and gives the quotient the sign of the two inputs combined.

name: exchange_value_through_helper
description: Reads a value into a local through a helper in mode zero, runs two further calls, then passes the local to the helper in mode one and returns it.

name: store_stack_value_via_helper
description: Passes a stack slot to a helper in mode one and returns.

name: transfer_saved_value
description: When the flag argument is zero, copies a global value into the target location. Otherwise it stores the value at the target into the global.

name: allocate_free_table_slot
description: Scans a table of 24-byte entries for one whose flag byte is clear, and passes the first free entry with its arguments to a routine. It returns zero when the table has no free entries.

name: call_routine_for_table_slot
description: Returns zero when the slot pointer is at the end of the table. Otherwise it passes the slot and two arguments to a routine.

name: forward_slot_arguments
description: Passes two arguments and the slot pointer from the frame to a routine, then returns.

name: open_file_by_mode_string
description: Parses a file mode string, choosing binary or append flags, then opens the file with a library call using a fixed permission value of 420. It returns null when the open fails.

name: open_file_for_mode_pointer
description: Parses a mode character and a following plus sign, then opens the file with the same flags and fixed permission value of 420. It returns null when the open fails.
